quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates, what should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way and don't need to check for trains.
You can pass slower drivers while crossing the tracks.
Make sure your vehicle can cross the tracks completely without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross the tracks completely without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before driving onto railroad tracks, check that you have enough room to cross completely. Never try to pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing any tracks.

questions.question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?

options.text: If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it is safe to drive.
If you are under the legal alcohol limit, your driving is not affected.
Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your judgment. Good judgment helps you react properly to things on the road. Even if you are below the legal limit, any alcohol will likely affect your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: Compared to daytime driving, night driving is:
questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous than daytime driving. It is harder to see in the dark. You can be blinded by other vehicles' lights. More tired or impaired drivers may be on the road at night.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, yield to any driver:
questions.correctAnswerText: Who arrived before you.
questions.explanation: After stopping, vehicles should go through a four-way stop in the order they arrived. If multiple vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: When driving past a vehicle that just parked on the roadside, you should:

options.text: Expect the driver to open the car door as you approach.
Assume the driver will wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the driver to open the car door as you approach.
questions.explanation: When passing a parked vehicle, assume the driver may open the door as you approach. Be extra careful when driving near parked cars.

questions.question: A five-sided sign is a:

options.text: School zone or school crossing sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone or school crossing sign.
questions.explanation: A five-sided sign warns drivers about school zones. Some signs show school crosswalks where children and pedestrians may be present.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is behind you on a city street. What should you do?

options.text: Drive to the right edge and slow down.
Drive to the right edge and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge and stop.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any emergency vehicle using lights and sirens. Drive to the right edge of the road and stop until it passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through first, then stop.

questions.question: A bicyclist who breaks traffic laws:

options.text: Does not have to follow traffic laws.
Will always get a warning from law enforcement.
Will have their bicycle taken away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be ticketed.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights, duties, and responsibilities as drivers. Both drivers and bicyclists who break traffic laws can receive tickets.

questions.question: Using a handheld phone to read, write, or send messages while driving is:

options.text: A secondary offense with a fine of $50 to $100.
A secondary offense with a fine of $200 to $500.
Not a traffic violation in Nebraska.

questions.correctAnswerText: A secondary offense with a fine of $200 to $500.
questions.explanation: Using a handheld phone to read, write, or send messages while driving is a secondary offense. The fine is $200 to $500.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.
questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce
questions.explanation: Slow down when turning. This lets you control your vehicle, stay in your lane, and handle unexpected situations.

questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes show arrows to control turns from specific lanes. A green arrow:

options.text: Is used only on one-way streets.
Means the same as a green light, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
Means you may go only if a green arrow appears with a circular green light.
Points the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: Means the same as a green light, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means the same as a circular green light. However, traffic in that lane must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you to stay on the right side of the divider ahead.

questions.question: If your turn signals fail, use ____ to show that you are turning.
questions.correctAnswerText: Hand signals
questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to tell other drivers you are about to turn.

questions.question: This yellow warning sign means:

options.text: You are approaching a school or school crosswalk.
Slow down, drive carefully, and watch for children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed near schools to warn drivers. It tells you to slow down, drive carefully, and watch for children.

questions.question: If you park facing uphill where there is no curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a road without a curb, turn your front wheels toward the edge of the road. This way, if the brakes fail, your car will roll off the road safely.

questions.question: You should always travel:

options.text: At the speed of the vehicles around you.
At a speed that fits the road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a speed that fits the road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Your driving speed depends on road conditions, weather, and the speed limit. Never drive faster than the legal speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Highway pavement is most slippery and dangerous:

options.text: If it has been raining for several hours.
If it has just started to rain.
If it has been raining for one to two hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: If it has just started to rain.
questions.explanation: Pavement is most slippery when rain first begins. Dirt and oil on the road mix with rainwater and create a slick layer.

questions.question: Sudden wind gusts on highways:

options.text: Can cause problems for all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause problems for all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind can affect all drivers. Wind can reduce visibility by blowing dust and dirt, and it can also physically push a vehicle sideways.

questions.question: When another driver is tailgating you:

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If no right lane is open, wait until the road ahead is clear, then slowly reduce speed to let the tailgater pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If being tailgated and a right lane is open, move over. If no right lane exists, wait until the road ahead is clear, then slowly reduce speed to encourage the other driver to pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of being hit from behind.

questions.question: Drivers may pass on a two-lane road with a single solid yellow line on their side.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: When there is a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line separating opposite traffic, you may only pass when the broken line is on your side.

questions.question: What color are warning signs for pedestrians, bicycles, playgrounds, schools, and school buses?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow-green
questions.explanation: Yellow-green signs warn you about pedestrians, bicycles, playgrounds, schools, and school buses. Watch carefully for pedestrians and children near these signs.

questions.question: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless:

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle can go fast enough to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe passing requires three things: you can see the road clearly, you can get back to your lane before oncoming traffic arrives, and your vehicle can go fast enough to pass. Only pass when it is safe and legal.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children:

options.text: Do not proceed until the children wave to you.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with its stop arm out and lights flashing, watch for children walking along the side of the road. Always drive carefully around children.

questions.question: A good rule to remember for passing is:

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when needed.
Try to get to the front of slow-moving traffic so you can see better.
Always flash your lights and sound your horn to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Each time you pass, you increase the chance of a collision. If you go faster than surrounding traffic, you will need to keep passing. Drive with traffic flow at the legal speed limit and only pass when necessary.

questions.question: If a transit vehicle is signaling to re-enter the main roadway after a stop, you must:

options.text: Honk to let them know you're there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any transit vehicle signaling to pull back onto the road after stopping to load or unload passengers. Slow down, change lanes, or stop to let the bus safely re-enter traffic.
